newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian, U.S. spacemen start six-hour spacewalk.
newsitem.headline: Russian, U.S. spacemen start six-hour spacewalk.

text.p: A Russian cosmonaut and a U.S. astronaut stepped out of the orbiting station Mir on Tuesday at the start of a space walk due to last about six hours, a mission control spokesman said.

"Vasiliy Tsibliev and NASA astronaut Jerry Linenger left Mir at 9.10 a.m. Moscow time (0510 GMT)," the spokesman told Reuters by telephone from the control centre in the town of Korolyov, outside Moscow.
The spacewalk, which is being videotaped from inside Mir by third crew member Alexander Lazutkin, had been due to begin 20 minutes earlier. The spokesman did not explain the delay.

He said the two men would dismantle equipment which collects samples of space dust outside the station. The equipment, set up a year ago, will then be brought back to Earth by the U.S. Shuttle spacecraft next month.
In the past few weeks the Mir crew members have faced several problems on the station, which has been in orbit for 11 years. These have included leaks in the cooling system and small fires.
Toilet tanks overflowed last year after delays in bringing supplies to the station and a new generator was hastily sent to Mir after problems with energy supplies.
